response: No, juvenile ankylosing spondylitis is not exactly the same disease as adult ankylosing spondylitis, although they share similar characteristics. Juvenile ankylosing spondylitis, also known as juvenile spondyloarthritis, tends to have a more varied presentation, often involving peripheral joints and entheses (where tendons and ligaments attach to bones), in addition to the spine. It may also have a stronger association with other conditions, such as inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis. The disease course and prognosis can differ between juvenile and adult forms, with juvenile onset often being more severe and having a greater impact on growth and development.
